title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
description: Ten named destinations on distinct blocks and corridors within Georgia Tech’s practical Atlanta orbit, each paired with one sourced reason to go.

cards.title: Browse Atlantic Station’s Full Directory
cards.subtitle: 17th Street corridor
cards.notes: Cross the 17th Street bridge and use the official directory to choose among the district’s shops, restaurants, services, and entertainment.
cards.short_summary: A directory-backed stop for combining several errands or activities in one district.
cards.evidence_claim: Atlantic Station’s official directory lists shopping, dining, entertainment, and services at 1380 Atlantic Drive NW, and Discover Atlanta locates the district off 17th Street.
cards.access_notes: The district is publicly accessible, but individual businesses set their own hours and may require purchases or tickets.

cards.title: See the Jim Henson Collection
cards.subtitle: Spring Street at 18th Street
cards.notes: Head to the bright-green building on Spring Street and plan time for the documented Jim Henson Collection or another current exhibition.
cards.short_summary: A museum-and-performance destination centered on puppetry and screen characters.
cards.evidence_claim: The Center for Puppetry Arts documents its Jim Henson Collection and gives its location as 1404 Spring Street NW at 18th Street.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday through Sunday according to the official site. Museum exhibitions and performances generally require tickets.

cards.title: Investigate Design at MODA
cards.subtitle: Peachtree Street at 16th Street
cards.notes: Walk into MODA’s street-level galleries and check the current exhibit listing before setting out, since its design program changes over time.
cards.short_summary: A compact Peachtree Street museum devoted entirely to design.
cards.evidence_claim: MODA states that it is a museum devoted to design, located at 1315 Peachtree Street NE and open Wednesday through Sunday.
cards.access_notes: The official site lists Wednesday-Sunday hours of noon-7 p.m.; verify admission and the current exhibition before visiting.

cards.title: Explore the High’s Art Galleries
cards.subtitle: Peachtree Street at 15th Street
cards.notes: Enter from the Woodruff Arts Center campus and use the High’s online maps to locate collection galleries and current special exhibitions.
cards.short_summary: A major collection-and-exhibition stop directly across from Arts Center MARTA.
cards.evidence_claim: The High documents historical and contemporary collection galleries, special exhibitions, visitor maps, and its address at 1280 Peachtree Street NE.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit - High Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday-Sunday with the last ticket issued one hour before closing; collection and most special-exhibition access is ticketed.

cards.title: Catch an Event on the Square
cards.subtitle: Peachtree Street at 14th Street
cards.notes: Check Colony Square’s event listings before walking over; its documented program includes outdoor yoga, movies, and live-music evenings.
cards.short_summary: An arts-infused Midtown complex with an actively programmed central square.
cards.evidence_claim: Colony Square’s official site lists Yoga on the Square, Movies on the Square, and Groovin’ on the Square at 1197 Peachtree Street NE.
cards.access_notes: The central complex is accessible to visitors; event schedules, registration requirements, and tenant hours vary.

cards.title: Tour or Attend the Fox Theatre
cards.subtitle: Peachtree Street at Ponce de Leon Avenue
cards.notes: Look up the current calendar, then choose a guided architectural tour, Broadway production, concert, comedy show, or film screening.
cards.short_summary: A historic movie palace offering tours and a broad live-performance calendar.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fox Theatre identifies its location at 660 Peachtree Street NE and invites visitors to take a guided tour, attend a concert, or see a Broadway play.
cards.access_notes: Building access depends on a scheduled tour or event; consult the official calendar and obtain the appropriate ticket.

cards.title: Take a Daylight Park Loop
cards.subtitle: 10th Street corridor
cards.notes: Enter near 10th Street, consult the conservancy map, and build a loop around named park features while following posted City of Atlanta rules.
cards.short_summary: A large city park with mapped paths, recreation areas, and visitor facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Piedmont Park Conservancy identifies Piedmont Park as a City of Atlanta park, provides a visitor map, and lists daily operating hours.
cards.access_notes: The conservancy lists park hours as 6 a.m.-11 p.m.; follow City of Atlanta park rules and posted event restrictions.

cards.title: Browse the Converted Industrial District
cards.subtitle: Howell Mill Road corridor
cards.notes: Start on Howell Mill Road and browse the linked buildings for furnishings, fashion, food, and other businesses listed by the district.
cards.short_summary: An adaptive-reuse retail district spread across several Howell Mill Road addresses.
cards.evidence_claim: Westside Provisions District’s official site describes retail focused on furnishings, fashion, and recreation at 1100-1210 Howell Mill Road.
cards.access_notes: The district can be browsed without a single admission ticket, but tenants maintain separate hours and most activities involve purchases.

cards.title: Walk Westside Paper’s Industrial Campus
cards.subtitle: West Marietta Street corridor
cards.notes: Enter from West Marietta Street and explore the mixed-use campus’s preserved industrial setting before consulting its current tenant directory.
cards.short_summary: A redeveloped paper-company site pairing historic industrial character with modern uses.
cards.evidence_claim: Westside Paper describes a 15-plus-acre mixed-use campus with a historic feel at 950 West Marietta Street NW.
cards.access_notes: Common areas and individual tenants may operate on different schedules; check the live directory before visiting.

cards.title: Follow the Directory Through The Works
cards.subtitle: Chattahoochee Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Use the directory to connect the food hall, shops, community art, dog park, and Woodall Rail Trail access across the property.
cards.short_summary: A large adaptive-reuse complex with food, retail, art, recreation, and trail access.
cards.evidence_claim: The Works’ official directory lists dining, shopping, community art, Westbound Dog Park, and Woodall Rail Trail at 1295 Chattahoochee Avenue.
cards.access_notes: The property lists daily hours of 7 a.m.-10 p.m.; individual shops vary, and purchases are required for commercial offerings.

warnings: Exact coordinates were left null because the cited destination pages did not publish verifiable latitude/longitude values.
Some destinations share the broader Peachtree Street spine but occupy distinct named blocks and have different sourced reasons to visit.
Travel distance and route conditions vary; consult current transit, pedestrian, and cycling information before leaving campus.
